chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Kirk's personnel and Mary Lou Williams' substitute chords
summary: He lists the Kirk trumpet and sax sections and learns substitute chords for 'Indiana' from Mary Lou Williams.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Who was in Kirk's band at that time?
Oh, they had Harold Baker, Big Jim Lawson and myself, and Bill Coleman...
Bill Coleman?
Yeah.
That's a good trumpet section.
Yeah, it was good. And Al Sears, Ben Smith, Harrington and John Williams.
Was that the alto player?
Harrington was their alto player.
Yeah, but John Williams played alto and baritone?
He played baritone.
That wasn't the same one that married Mary Lou Williams.
Yeah, that was the same one. But she was going with Harold Baker at that time.
Uh-huh. Now, was she in the band?
Yeah, she was in the band. Her and Booker Collins.
Booker Collins. And Ben Thigpen?
Yeah, and Thigpen. That's the first time I'd ever worked with any name band.
So that was the first time you met Mary Lou.
Yeah.
She must have been quite impressive.

Oh, she was. I went to her and asked her what do you use for chords, like, to play when you play "Indiana," and she showed me like where you put in the substitute chords like A-flat, G-flat, F-7 to B-flat, instead of going [DE-DA-DA-DA] and then go to F-7, DE-DA-DA-DA, and then go to B-flat-7, and each change you add that F-sharp in there...
Was she the first one that...
That hipped me to that.
That showed you those kind of things.
Those kinds of things, yeah. You know, I didn't know you could do that even with music. I found out you could.
